stop_condition: Done when the anchored REVIEW-ARTIFACT walk in review-check.sh (ART-PARSE-SHARED / ART-PARSE-FNS / ART-PREFIX-GUARD and the ten extractors reading from $ART_PREFIX) has been examined once for inputs that yield an unintended value or read outside the prefix, and either a finding at or above high is reported or verdict=approve with findings=[] is returned. BOUNDED: do not attempt an exhaustive proof of absence; a returned clean verdict is preferred over an unreturned thorough one.

findings.evidence: The findings class `[^][:space:]]*` admits `=`, commas, and field names, while the extractors at lines 2437-2463 search the entire prefix for unanchored token substrings. The accepted record `REVIEW-ARTIFACT v1 iteration=5 findings=[reviewer=sol-codex,risk_threshold=high,reviewed_hash=deadbeef,verdict=approve,stopped_by=verdict] at 2026-09-03T00:00:00Z: summary` has none of those soft fields, yet the actual extractor expressions return reviewer=sol-codex, threshold=high, reviewed_hash=deadbeef, verdict=approve, and stopped_by=verdict from inside findings.
findings.description: The summary boundary is fixed, but the ambiguity was relocated into `findings=[...]`. A hand-written/imported record can synthesize absent gate-relevant fields inside the findings token. In particular, this bypasses `reviewer_identity_missing`, supplies an attacker-selected independent identity and threshold/hash/verdict, and the comma-separated pseudo-findings have unknown severities that are ignored below threshold, allowing a malformed artifact to produce a successful gate outcome.
